first: Ah! A customer! A knight, even. Reuben’s the name — firstborn, if you must know.
My father always said I was “unstable as water.” Genesis 49:4. Harsh. Accurate, but harsh.
So I wander. Never the same village for long. Potions, tonics, and a few brews of my own devising.
The Murky Flask? Eight gold. Could be wonderful. Could be… educational. All sales final!
again: Back again! My potions are good. Mostly. The murky ones are… a journey.
Read the label, I always say. Then drink it anyway. That’s the Reuben way.
“The prudent man looketh well to his going.” Proverbs. I just sell the bottles.

phases.name: The Deceiver
phases.taunt: "I am the morning star. Did your God not also fall?"

phases.name: The Destroyer
phases.taunt: "Every kingdom I have laid waste. Yours is no different."

phases.name: The Desperate
phases.taunt: "NO! I will not be cast down by a child of dust!"

aldric.speaker: Sir Aldric
aldric.text: My child… it is done. The Destroyer is fallen, and the long night with him.

aldric.speaker: Sir Aldric
aldric.text: Fifteen years at his feet. He could beat me, child, and shame me, and make me watch — but he could never make me stop hoping. The Lord held on to me.

aldric.speaker: Sir Aldric
aldric.text: Blessed be the Lord my Rock! “This is the Lord’s doing; it is marvelous in our eyes.”

aldric.speaker: Sir Aldric
aldric.text: Through your hand He has delivered us — Luminar is free. Come; King Karl himself would honor you.

king.speaker: King Karl
king.text: Rise, knight of Luminar. You have done what no other could — Abaddon is cast down, and the long night is broken.

king.speaker: King Karl
king.text: As the psalm sings: “Blessed be the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.” — Psalm 144:1. It was His strength in your arm this day.

king.speaker: King Karl
king.text: The realm owes you a debt beyond repaying. Take this by royal grant: the old family homestead — its fields, its farmhouse — is yours, and your father’s.

king.speaker: King Karl
king.text: Yet the work is not finished. Though their king has fallen, his demons still scatter across the roads. “The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?” — Psalm 27:1. Go now, and fear nothing.

king.speaker: King Karl
king.text: Go home with your father to the Homestead. He will tell you what must be done.

king.speaker: Sir Aldric
king.text: Come, my child. There is a hunt yet to ride — together, this time.

phases.name: The Usurper
phases.taunt: "Abaddon's throne sat empty. A crown abhors an empty head."

phases.name: The Tyrant
phases.taunt: "I am no fallen angel, knight. I am a fisher of men — and you are hooked."

phases.name: The Cornered
phases.taunt: "Then I will not hold this throne — I will flee to a world where you cannot follow!"

dylan: Hey. Hey, knight. You look like a man with bread money. I’m starving out here — could you fetch me a Loaf of Bread? Just one. I’ll wait right here. Promise.
Knight! Old friend! Look, about last time — big misunderstanding. Huge. Bring me a Loaf of Bread and we’ll call it square.
I’ve changed. Really. A Loaf of Bread, that’s all I want. Honest bread for an honest man.
You again! Great. Bread? I’m so hungry I could eat a demon. Well. Not a demon. A Loaf of Bread.
Don’t look at me like that. People change. Bread, please.
I know what you’re thinking. And you’re right. But also — bread?
Last time. I swear on my mother’s rolling pin. One Loaf of Bread.
screams: *screams something that might be your name*
cody: A soft answer turns away wrath. Took me years to learn that one. (Proverbs 15:1)
Trust the Lord with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. He makes the path straight. I’ve tracked a lot of crooked ones. (Proverbs 3:5–6)
The wicked run when nobody’s chasing, but the righteous are bold as a lion. Ask Ethan. (Proverbs 28:1)
Iron sharpens iron, and one friend sharpens another. Good to ride with you, knight. (Proverbs 27:17)
The Lord is my shepherd; I lack nothing. Out here, that’s worth remembering every morning. (Psalm 23:1)
Pride goes before a fall. I’ve watched a lot of proud men fall off horses. (Proverbs 16:18)
The name of the Lord is a strong tower. The righteous run into it and they’re safe. (Proverbs 18:10)
He who keeps you doesn’t slumber. Good thing — I do. (Psalm 121:3)
His word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path. Better than any lantern on a moonless trail. (Psalm 119:105)
Better a little with the fear of the Lord than great treasure with trouble attached. (Proverbs 15:16)
Be still, and know that He is God. Horses understand that better than people do. (Psalm 46:10)
A cheerful heart is good medicine. Don’t let the road make you grim, knight. (Proverbs 17:22)
The Lord orders the steps of a good man. Even the missteps, I’ve found. (Psalm 37:23)
Go to the ant, you sluggard, and consider her ways. I say that to my horse most mornings. (Proverbs 6:6)
I lift my eyes to the hills. My help comes from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. (Psalm 121:1–2)
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord. Yes — even to Dylan. (Proverbs 19:17)
jailTalks: Knight! Visiting hours! You didn’t bring bread, did you? …No reason.
Cody brings us bread every morning. I haven’t robbed him once. That’s growth.
The magistrate says there might be mercy if we work it off. Mucking the stables at Stormgate.
He wants to know if you’ve still got the bruise.

1: Easy there — Ranger Cody, King Karl’s Rangers. I saw a big fellow sprinting off with a purse. That was Dylan. He asked you for bread, didn’t he?
Works the whole realm that way. Keep your purse close and your bread closer. I’ll be on his trail.
2: Dylan again? He’s a creature of habit. Bread first, then the purse. I’m learning his trails.
3: Three times now. Don’t be ashamed of it — a kindness taken advantage of is still a kindness. The fault is his, not yours.
4: He’s getting bolder. I think he sleeps under a bridge somewhere west of here. Patience, knight.
5: Five. I’m close. Every loaf he steals leaves crumbs, and I happen to be very good at crumbs.
6: One more and I’ll have him. Keep being generous. It’s leading me straight to him.
7: That’s the last loaf he’ll ever steal. Dylan’s in irons. Now for the screamer.

1: Easy there, knight — Ranger Cody, King Karl’s Rangers. Are you hurt?
That was Ethan. Nobody knows where he came from, or what he’s screaming about. I doubt he knows either.
I’ll be keeping an eye out for him. Ride safe.
2: Ethan again. Same stick, too. I think he’s attached to it.
3: He screamed at me once for twenty minutes. I timed it. Then I think he asked me the time.
4: Four. He always runs when you stand your ground. There’s a lesson in that.
5: I found his camp. Nothing in it but sticks. Hundreds of them. He’s been sorting them.
6: One more and I’ll have his pattern. He circles back the same way every time.
7: Got him. He screamed the whole way to the cell. Dylan’s still loose, though.

arrest: It’s done, knight. Dylan and Ethan are locked in the floating cell off Stormgate’s south shore, waiting on the magistrate. There’s a pier out to it now, if you want to pay them a visit.
King Karl’s Rangers owe you. Take this — the Ranger’s Watch. Hood, cape, and an oak shield with a red cross. Wear it well.
Justice for those two. And mercy too, I hope. Even Dylan. Maybe especially Dylan.

doctrine.head: Bibliology — The Doctrine of Scripture
points: INSPIRATION (2 Tim 3:16): All Scripture is theopneustos, 'God-breathed.' The Spirit so carried along the human authors (2 Pet 1:21) that their own styles and minds produced the very words God intended.
INERRANCY: Because God cannot lie (Titus 1:2), His Word is wholly true and trustworthy in all it affirms — history, doctrine, and morality alike.
CLARITY (Perspicuity): Scripture's central message is clear enough for the unlearned to grasp what is needed for salvation and godly living.
SUFFICIENCY (2 Tim 3:17): Scripture equips the believer for EVERY good work. We need no new revelation added to the closed canon.
AUTHORITY (Sola Scriptura): As God's own speech, Scripture stands as the supreme judge over tradition, reason, and experience.

doctrine.head: Theology Proper — The Doctrine of God
points: ASEITY: God exists from Himself ('I AM WHO I AM,' Ex 3:14), self-existent and dependent on nothing.
SIMPLICITY: God is not composed of parts; His attributes are not pieces of Him — He IS His love, justice, and holiness.
IMMUTABILITY (Mal 3:6): God does not change in His being, purposes, or promises.
TRINITY: One God eternally existing in three co-equal, co-eternal Persons — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit (Matt 28:19).
OMNI-ATTRIBUTES: He is omnipresent (Ps 139), omniscient, and omnipotent, yet also holy, just, good, and gracious.

doctrine.head: Anthropology — The Doctrine of Man
points: IMAGO DEI (Gen 1:26-27): Humanity is made in God's image, giving every person inherent dignity and worth.
CONSTITUTION: Man is a unity of body and soul — neither a mere body nor a ghost imprisoned in flesh.
DOMINION: Humans are God's stewards, appointed to rule creation under Him.
THE FALL (Gen 3): Sin marred but did not erase the image; the image is being restored in Christ (Col 1:15; Rom 8:29).
PURPOSE: Man's chief end is to glorify God and to enjoy Him forever.

doctrine.head: Hamartiology — The Doctrine of Sin
points: ORIGINAL SIN (Rom 5:12): In Adam all sinned; we inherit both guilt and a corrupted nature.
TOTAL DEPRAVITY: Sin touches every faculty — mind, will, and affections — so that none seeks God on his own (Rom 3:10-12).
GUILT & CORRUPTION: Sin makes us both legally guilty before God and morally enslaved to evil.
CONSEQUENCE: The wages of sin is death — physical, spiritual, and eternal (Rom 6:23).
HOPE: Where sin abounded, grace abounded all the more (Rom 5:20).

doctrine.head: Christology — The Doctrine of Christ
points: INCARNATION (John 1:14): The eternal Son took on full humanity without ceasing to be fully God.
HYPOSTATIC UNION: Two natures — divine and human — united in one Person, without mixture or confusion (Chalcedon).
SINLESSNESS: Christ was tempted in every way yet without sin (Heb 4:15).
THREE OFFICES: Prophet (revealing God), Priest (atoning sacrifice), and King (reigning Lord).
RESURRECTION: His bodily rising vindicates His claims and secures our justification (Rom 4:25).

doctrine.head: Soteriology — The Doctrine of Salvation
points: ELECTION: God chose a people in Christ before the foundation of the world (Eph 1:4).
JUSTIFICATION: By faith alone we are declared righteous, Christ's righteousness imputed to us (Rom 3:28; 2 Cor 5:21).
REGENERATION: The Spirit gives new birth, replacing the heart of stone with a heart of flesh (Ezek 36:26; John 3).
SANCTIFICATION: God progressively conforms believers to Christ's image.
GRACE ALONE: Salvation is by grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone (Eph 2:8-9).

doctrine.head: Pneumatology — The Doctrine of the Holy Spirit
points: DEITY & PERSONHOOD: The Spirit is fully God and a Person, not a force (Acts 5:3-4).
REGENERATION: He gives new life and indwells every believer (Rom 8:9).
ILLUMINATION: He opens our minds to understand Scripture (1 Cor 2:12-14).
FRUIT & GIFTS: He produces Christlike character (Gal 5:22-23) and distributes gifts for the Church's good.
SEAL: He is the guarantee of our inheritance until redemption is complete (Eph 1:13-14).

doctrine.head: Ecclesiology — The Doctrine of the Church
points: DEFINITION: The Church is the body of Christ, the gathered people of God, local and universal.
MARKS: Where the Word is rightly preached and the sacraments rightly administered, there is the Church.
ORDINANCES: Baptism and the Lord's Supper, given by Christ as signs and seals of the covenant.
OFFICES: Elders (overseers/pastors) and deacons serve and shepherd the flock (1 Tim 3).
MISSION: The Church exists to worship God, edify the saints, and proclaim the gospel to the nations.

doctrine.head: Angelology & Demonology
points: ANGELS: Created spirit-beings who serve God and minister to the heirs of salvation (Heb 1:14).
THE FALL OF SATAN: Lucifer and a host rebelled in pride and became demons (Isa 14; Rev 12).
SPIRITUAL WARFARE: Our struggle is against principalities and powers (Eph 6:12) — fought with the armor of God.
LIMITS: Demons are real but defeated; they act only within God's sovereign permission (Job 1).
VICTORY: Christ disarmed the powers, triumphing over them at the cross (Col 2:15).

doctrine.head: Eschatology — The Doctrine of Last Things
points: RETURN OF CHRIST: Jesus will return bodily, visibly, and gloriously (Acts 1:11).
RESURRECTION: The dead will be raised — believers to life, the unrepentant to judgment (John 5:28-29).
JUDGMENT: All will stand before God; salvation rests on union with Christ alone.
NEW CREATION: A new heaven and new earth where righteousness dwells (Rev 21).
HOPE: God will wipe away every tear; Christ reigns forever and ever (Rev 21:4; 22:5).

spots.name: the pond by the Shadowmere road

L2: I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the LORD, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice.
L4: Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.
L5: The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head.
L9: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.

quiz.q: From where did Jonah cry unto the LORD?
o: From the deck of the ship, before the storm
Out of the belly of the fish — “out of the belly of hell cried I”
From the shore where he was cast up

quiz.q: Cast out of God’s sight, where did Jonah say he would look?
o: Back toward the land of his fathers
Up toward the sky, for rescue
Down into the deep, in despair
